title: Exact induction and injective restriction for condensed product actions
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $G,H$ be profinite groups. For $P=1,G,H,G\times H$, let $\mathcal A_P(A)$ be the category of internal $A$-modules with an $A$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline P$, with the inflation adjunctions of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Internal modules are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; write $U_P:\mathcal A_P(A)\to\mathcal A_1(A)$ for forgetting the action, $A[S]$ for the free internal module on a profinite set $S$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction], and $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ for the internal module Hom [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].
For every profinite $S$, the module $A[S]$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}A(V)$ and is flat: $A[S]\otimes_A-$ is exact. The equivalence with sectionwise module sheaves preserves these tensor and internal-Hom operations. The functors $U_P$ and restriction $\operatorname{Res}_H:\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)\to\mathcal A_H(A)$ preserve and reflect exactness. The exact left adjoint of $U_P$ is $M\mapsto A[P]\otimes_AM$ with translation action; the exact left adjoint of $\operatorname{Res}_H$ is $M\mapsto A[G]\otimes_AM$ with translation by $G$ and the given $H$-action on $M$. Its adjunction sends $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}_H X$ to $[g]\otimes m\mapsto g f(m)$. In particular these restriction and forgetful functors preserve injective objects.
For every $N\in\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$ a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ exists. For any such resolution, $U_{G\times H}I^q$ and $\operatorname{Res}_H I^q$ are injective, while $(I^q)^H$ is injective in $\mathcal A_G(A)$ and $U_G((I^q)^H)$ is injective in $\mathcal A_1(A)$. Both $I^\bullet$ and $(I^\bullet)^H$ are K-injective in their respective action categories; $(I^\bullet)^H$ represents $R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$ in $D(\mathcal A_G(A))$, without requiring it to resolve $N^H[0]$. These assertions include trivial groups, the empty profinite set, zero modules and the zero ring.

proof.text:
Let $E$ be the internal-to-sectionwise module equivalence. The site's size hypothesis and strong monoidal abelian sheafification are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], so [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], $E$ is exact and identifies relative tensors by the local formula $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$. It also identifies internal Homs: [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] and [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] give the two tensor-Hom adjunctions, and for each test module $T$ they identify
$\operatorname{Hom}(T,E\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(M,N))=\operatorname{Hom}(E^{-1}T\otimes_A M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes_A EM,EN)$.
The representing isomorphism and its inverse are the maps corresponding to the identity maps under these natural bijections; their composites are identities by the same bijections. Thus the comparison preserves the internal-Hom operation, including its evaluation map.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product), 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); internal comparison is the agent argument using the cited equivalence.

proof.text: For a profinite $S$, put $B(V)=A(V)$ and $E_S(V)=C(V,S)$. The sheafification of $V\mapsto B(V)[E_S(V)]$ is the free module on $E_S$ by [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property]. Comparing its generator adjunction with [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction] identifies it with the sectionwise realization of $A[S]$: both inverse comparison maps send $[s]$ to $[s]$. Its displayed presheaf is precisely $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to S}A(V)$. Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat] to the ringed profinite site and its object $S$; this sheaf is $j_{S!}B_S$ and its tensor functor is exact. Transport along the exact tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] proves internal flatness of $A[S]$. No constancy assumption on the condensed ring has been used.

Use CondensedDerivedRestriction.forgetExact of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants] for forgetting each action: it preserves finite limits and colimits and detects exactness. For product restriction, restrictionLimits and restrictionColimits give preservation; apply forgetExact first to the product-action complex and then to its H-restriction. The underlying module complexes agree definitionally, hence their exactness equivalences prove reflection as well.

source.place: Tag 03CX (section-sheafification), exact module sheafification; the kernel and quotient action formulas are the agent argument.

proof.text: Apply ProductForgetting.exists_datum of [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting] to the profinite first group and profinite retained group. For the plain induction choose both groups equal to P and use plainInduction; for the product induction use G,H and induction. The recorded freeGroup and generator are definitionally restrictionFree and restrictionGenerator, and forgetFirst is restriction along inr. Copy the underlying tensor comparison, additive functor, exactness and normalized adjunction. For the translation formula, apply the inverse underlying comparison to its recorded action equation and cancel hom followed by inv on sections. For product actions write p=(fst p,snd p), using extensionality of continuous maps, before the same cancellation. The inverse-transpose formulas agree definitionally. These are local existential witnesses inside the proofs, never data definitions chosen from unproved existence.

source.place: Agent construction of internal induction from the two cited universal properties; blueprint paragraph (3), formal internal-bar input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to each exact induction adjunction of step 4. Its left adjoint preserves monomorphisms because it is exact, so $U_P$ and $\operatorname{Res}_H$ preserve injectives. For $F=(-)^H:\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)\to\mathcal A_G(A)$, [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants] supplies the exact left adjoint, inflation along $G\times H\to G$. The same right-adjoint lemma shows that $F$ preserves injectives. Consequently if $J$ is injective with product action, $U_{G\times H}J$, $\operatorname{Res}_H J$ and $J^H$ are injective; applying the already established result for $U_G$ to $J^H$ shows that $U_G(J^H)$ is injective as well. In the Lean assembly, the exactness instance for projection inflation is the existing restrictionLimits theorem of def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants. The two preceding induction theorems supply precisely their injective-preservation conjuncts; no induction witness is selected in a definition.

Use the existing abelian and Grothendieck action-category instances of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]. Mathlib IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives ([lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]) supplies enough injectives, and injectiveResolution N ([lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]) gives a nonnegative resolution of every N. For any supplied resolution I, InjectiveResolution.cochainComplex extends it by zero to integer degrees and its existing instances give injective terms in every degree, including negative ones. Apply the three injective-preservation results of step 5 to each term, then apply forgetting for G to the invariant term. This proves all four asserted injectivities.

source.place: Tag 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), clause (1); enough injectives is Tag 079H (injectives.tex, theorem-injective-embedding-grothendieck).

proof.text: The original resolution complex is K-injective by the existing Mathlib instance for InjectiveResolution.cochainComplex. Its termwise V-image is strictly supported in degrees at least zero, since the additive functor preserves zero objects. Step 5 makes all its terms injective. Apply CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective at the bound zero ([lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]). For the total derived comparison, use the proved source-library definition Functor.rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso on I.cochainComplex: it is the inverse right-derived unit, with the quotient-to-derived comparison isomorphisms. Compose it with the image under V.functor.rightDerivedFunctor of DerivedCategory.singleFunctorIsoCompQ at N followed by asIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map I.ι'). The map I.ι' is a quasi-isomorphism by the injective-resolution API, so this is an isomorphism. The resulting endpoints are exactly RF(N[0]) and Q(F(I)). No quasi-isomorphism from N^H[0] to the invariant complex is asserted or used. The broader kInjective_computes theorem about homotopy categories and ordinary derived cohomology is not needed.

source.place: Tag 013R (lemma-acyclic-is-zero), bounded-below injectives; Tags 070H and 070I (definition-K-injective and lemma-K-injective), computation in the unbounded derived category.

proof.text: For a trivial group the induction formulas reduce to $A[1]\otimes_A M=A\otimes_A M\cong M$ and invariants are the identity. For $S=\varnothing$, the displayed free presheaf is zero on nonempty test objects and is also zero on the empty test object, since $A(\varnothing)=0$ by the empty-cover sheaf condition; hence $A[\varnothing]=0$ and its tensor functor is exact. For a zero module all maps and actions above are the unique zero maps. Over the zero ring every unital module is zero, so its action categories have one object up to unique isomorphism and all assertions hold. The proofs used neither nontriviality of groups nor nonzero coefficients.
